Indexed replicated log and snapshot boundary

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft main loop and one RPC goroutine per remote voter
behaviors.protocol_context: Local current term and latest voter configuration
behaviors.trigger: Follower contact timeout, campaign retry, pre-vote success or TimeoutNow
implementation_guards: Known configuration and local voter status gate timeout elections. Pre-vote is optional and bypassed for leadership transfer.
Vote handler checks candidate membership, known leader/transfer exception, term, voter status, durable prior vote, then lexicographic last-log term/index.
reads: getLastEntry selects the last log when its index equals or exceeds snapshot index; otherwise the snapshot index/term supplies vote freshness.
writes: Current term is persisted before in-memory update. Vote term then candidate are persisted before granting.
Campaign-local response channel counts votes only from requested voters; fresh campaign channels isolate previous replies.
external_effects: A majority of granted votes sets Leader; higher response term sets Follower.
Transfer waits for replication nextIndex to pass lastIndex, then sends TimeoutNow; recipient starts transfer-marked candidacy.
async_boundaries: RequestVote RPCs complete on the channel allocated to their campaign.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Election log freshness checks and term-specific ownership constrain which history can form later decisions.

unknowns: Crash/error behavior between the separate vote-term and vote-candidate writes is not yet resolved.

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft main loop with captured replication state
behaviors.trigger: Election enters runLeader; state change exits leaderLoop
implementation_guards: Lease check steps down without contact to a voter quorum. Newer replication reply term notifies this tenure's stepDown channel.
writes: Create new commitment, notification, inflight and replication objects at entry; emit current-term no-op.
On exit close replication stop channels, fail inflight and verify futures, and clear leader-owned pointers.
async_boundaries: Old replication workers retain their old commitment and stepDown objects, even after the main loop installs new ones.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Old replies can update old accounting but cannot directly count toward a new tenure's commitment object.

behaviors.execution_owner: Leader main loop and synchronized commitment object
behaviors.protocol_context: Leader tenure and latest voter set
behaviors.trigger: StoreLogs success, successful replication/snapshot acknowledgement, or configuration replacement
implementation_guards: match accepts only configured voter IDs and monotonically increasing indexes.
Majority order statistic must reach startIndex (first new entry of this tenure).
writes: Per-voter match indexes and commitment commitIndex.
Leader commitCh consumption updates Raft commitIndex, committed configuration and queues committed inflight logs.
external_effects: Local StoreLogs failure responds to affected futures and steps down.
async_boundaries: commitCh notification coalesces; main loop reads current commitment index.

cross_activity_effects.A5: Committed inflight ranges are passed to processLogs.
cross_activity_effects.A4: Committing local removal causes shutdown or follower transition.

behaviors.execution_owner: One follower replication goroutine plus optional pipeline decoder
behaviors.protocol_context: Captured leader term and tenure commitment object; peer identity
behaviors.trigger: Log trigger, CommitTimeout, deferred transfer trigger or retry
reads: Leader commit index, leader log/snapshot, follower nextIndex and request-associated replies.
writes: Requests advertise full leader commit index but cap Entries to MaxAppendEntries.
Reject reduces nextIndex by at least one, bounded by response LastLog+1 and 1. Success advances nextIndex to last sent entry+1 and reports its index.
important_branches: Missing retained log invokes snapshot transfer. Snapshot success reports snapshot index.
Higher response term stops replication and notifies stepDown. Pipeline failure falls back to ordinary replication.
Heartbeat requests have no entries, previous index or advertised commit index, and do not report log matches.
Snapshot success sets nextIndex to snapshot index+1; setPreviousLog uses snapshot term when nextIndex-1 equals the leader snapshot boundary.
async_boundaries: Pipelined replies refer to their associated requests. Heartbeats run separately from disk-bound replication.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Higher reply term challenges leadership; captured objects isolate tenure accounting.
cross_activity_effects.A3: Backtracking and snapshot fallback repair lagging followers.

unknowns: Can a legal history leave nextIndex before an already matching prefix with a divergent suffix when a later request advertises commitment beyond its bounded batch? Backtracking may exclude the simple proposed history.

behaviors.execution_owner: RPC handler through main loop; heartbeat callback may be concurrent
behaviors.protocol_context: Receiver current term, retained log and snapshot prefix
implementation_guards: Reject older term; update term/step down for newer request, with same-term leadership-transfer exception.
Verify previous log term; compare received entries, truncate at first conflict and persist replacement before success.
Previous-entry validation calls getLastEntry; equal cached log and snapshot indexes choose the cached log term. Otherwise a non-last previous entry is read from LogStore.
writes: A truncation crossing latest configuration rolls back to committed configuration.
Advance commitIndex to min(LeaderCommitIndex, getLastIndex()) if advertised index is greater, then processLogs.
durable_effects: Delete conflicting suffix and StoreLogs new entries.
external_effects: Success after application is queued; set last contact.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Incoming eligible-term request changes role and known leader.
cross_activity_effects.A5: Chosen commit bound controls logs sent to application.

unknowns: Whether producer history always makes the local-last-index commitment bound safe when an incoming batch ends before a retained suffix.
DeleteRange success followed by StoreLogs failure leaves the cached last log stale according to the local TODO; permitted error recovery remains open.
Successful snapshot boundary can coexist with an older cached term at the same index; legal producer history and scoped responsibility need separate attribution from this source observation.

behaviors.execution_owner: Leader main loop; follower append and startup scan
behaviors.protocol_context: Latest and committed configurations with indexes
behaviors.trigger: Configuration change request or configuration log read
implementation_guards: Admit leader changes only when latest is committed and current-term startIndex has committed.
Optional prevIndex must equal latest index; no duplicate IDs/addresses, empty IDs/addresses or zero-voter result.
writes: AddVoter directly sets Voter; dispatch configuration entry then set latest, reset voter eligibility and start/stop replication.
Rollback to committed on truncation; startup and incoming logs reconstruct configurations.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Latest voters determine support aggregation; retained voter IDs retain their match indexes.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Latest voters determine campaign electorate and local eligibility.

unknowns: Public AddVoter API promises staging until ready; ConfigurationChangeCommand documentation and configuration tests explicitly specify direct Voter creation. The proposal alone is not authoritative; the current source conflict remains unresolved.
Address changes and removed-then-readded identities need separate history analysis.

behaviors.execution_owner: Startup constructor, main RPC loop, snapshot worker and FSM worker
behaviors.protocol_context: Snapshot index/term/configuration and retained log suffix
behaviors.trigger: Startup, missing-log replication fallback or snapshot request
implementation_guards: Startup restores newest usable snapshot or fails when all existing snapshots fail; optional caller setting skips FSM restore.
Snapshot receiver rejects older terms, validates version and received size, finalizes snapshot then waits for FSM restore completion.
Snapshot creation obtains FSM snapshot and committed configuration; rejects snapshot index behind committed configuration index.
writes: Restore updates lastApplied, snapshot boundary and latest/committed configuration. Startup scans remaining log configurations.
Log compaction follows persisted snapshot; monotonic stores instead remove old logs after installation.
Successful installSnapshot stores supplied snapshot index/term after actual FSM restore, but does not update lastLog cache. Nonmonotonic-store compaction retains a configured tail of log entries.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Successful snapshot receipt contributes snapshot-index support to captured leader accounting.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Restored history bounds vote freshness and available authority context.
cross_activity_effects.A5: FSM Restore replaces state before receiver reports snapshot success.

unknowns: When a snapshot supersedes the cached last log at an equal index with a different term, can the sender repair subsequent rejection without another state change?
Administrative user restore and disaster RecoverCluster have distinct contracts not yet mapped.

behaviors.protocol_context: Node-local durable term, vote and indexed history
behaviors.trigger: Term/vote update, log write and startup
writes: Persist current term before publishing it; persist vote term and candidate before grant.
StoreLogs precedes local support and append success. NewRaft reads persisted term and last log then snapshot/configuration history.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Storage completion is the producer premise for match reporting.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Persisted votes constrain repeated grants and history determines election freshness.

unknowns: External durable backend behavior on partial errors is unspecified by these observations; InmemStore is explicitly test-only.

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft main loop queues; FSM worker consumes
behaviors.protocol_context: Per-node committed prefix and FIFO mutation queue
behaviors.trigger: Leader commit notification or follower commit propagation
implementation_guards: processLogs skips indexes at or below lastApplied; prepares command/barrier and supported configuration entries.
writes: lastApplied records queued progress, not necessarily completed FSM.Apply.
FSM worker executes command callbacks sequentially and completes associated future afterward.
async_boundaries: fsmMutateCh separates queue admission from callback completion.

cross_activity_effects.A7: ApplyFuture response is supplied after callback completion; leadership-loss result is independently uncertain.

implementation_guards: Enqueue timeout covers admission, not a numeric consensus completion deadline. Nonleaders reject.
external_effects: Leadership loss reports an error without guaranteeing the entry will not survive; successful future follows callback.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Admitted commands become term/index-stamped log entries under the leader.

facts.meaning: This tenure commitment object has a voter-majority match bound at or beyond its first new entry; main-loop consumption publishes that bound as the leader commit index.
facts.validity_context: Latest voter set and this tenure's startIndex; match indexes represent successful storage/replication reports, not FSM completion.
facts.durability: Commit accounting is volatile; underlying log entries are stored before reports.
facts.recovery: A new leader reconstructs support in a fresh object; persisted log/snapshot survives.

facts.meaning: The receiver selected an application bound from the advertised leader commit index and its local last index after append validation and any received-entry reconciliation.
facts.validity_context: Accepted AppendEntries term and current local history; the selected bound is not itself proof that every retained entry agrees with the sender.
facts.durability: Volatile commit index; selected entries reside in LogStore or restored snapshot history.
facts.recovery: Startup restores snapshot application boundary; later leader propagation or new leadership supplies further commitment.
unknowns: Does the composed sender/retry/history mechanism exclude a divergent retained suffix below this selected bound?

facts.meaning: A stored/restored snapshot identifies the included log prefix through its supplied last index and term; successful receiver installation has completed FSM Restore and published that boundary.
facts.validity_context: Successfully finalized and restored snapshot; its boundary coexists with any physically retained log entries and does not by itself assert that the last-log cache was rewritten.
facts.durability: Snapshot bytes and metadata are finalized in SnapshotStore; in-memory boundary is published after restore. Durability depends on configured store; test store is in-memory.
facts.recovery: NewRaft restores a usable snapshot and its index/term before scanning later configuration logs.
unknowns: Whether all consumers honor the installed boundary when physically retained old entries conflict.

surfaces.reason: Can a legal bounded request commit a retained divergent suffix? Ordinary backtracking is counterevidence, and producer history remains unresolved.
What responsibility applies after truncation succeeds and StoreLogs fails with cached lastLog unchanged?
Caller-authorized history replacement and disaster recovery need separate contract analysis; ordinary snapshot transfer is mapped.
Does predecessor validation consume the restored snapshot boundary rather than a superseded equal-index log term?
AppendFuture.Response is valid only after successful Error(), but pipelineDecode omits Error. Determine a permitted producer failure and actual consequence.

formation.explanation: Leader stamps admitted commands with term/index and stores them. Local storage and successful peer append/snapshot replies report match indexes into a tenure-owned object. Latest voters supply majority support, gated by a current-term entry. commitCh consumption publishes commitment, commits configurations and queues inflight logs. Replication advertises commitment; follower validates term/previous history, reconciles received conflicts and selects a local application bound. FSM queueing and callback completion are separate; commands complete their futures after callbacks.

context.explanation: Contact timeout starts eligible voter campaigning, optionally via pre-vote. Durable term/vote records, membership and lexicographic log freshness govern voting; campaign-local channels aggregate granted votes. New leadership creates a new commitment object and no-op. Higher terms, lease failure or committed removal end authority. Leadership transfer catches a selected peer up then triggers a transfer-marked campaign. Leader exit stops replication and fails pending futures without promising their entries cannot survive.

connection.explanation: Log freshness protects the history carried into new authority; persistence and snapshot restoration retain history across restart. A new tenure does not reuse the old quorum tracker: old replies reference old objects, while preserved log entries require fresh support reaching a new-term entry. Configuration controls both votes and match eligibility; new changes wait for previous commitment and current-term commitment. Followers preserve matching prefixes and reconcile received conflicts; prior queued application is not undone by leader transitions. The adequacy of the follower commit bound is a local unresolved relationship rather than assumed safety.

open_details: Follower commit-boundary question retains ordinary backtracking counterevidence; recovery histories remain distinct.
Installed snapshot boundary can conflict with equal-index cached log term; obligation concerns predecessor validation, not a presumed infinite stall.
AddVoter staging contract conflicts with command documentation and tests; pipeline response-error handling remains open.
Storage partial errors, administrative restore and legacy/transport variants remain open.
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation and authority lifecycles, their shared history/eligibility mechanisms, old-work handling and asynchronous consumption have been traced. Usable is a navigation judgment, not correctness or exhaustive coverage.
